title: Negotiations on Treaty on Conservation and Sustainable Use of Marine Biodiversity of Areas Beyond National Jurisdiction
what_it_is: Negotiations on Treaty on Conservation and Sustainable Use of Marine Biodiversity of Areas Beyond National Jurisdiction

sections.label: BBNJ Treaty under UN Convention
sections.summary: The BBNJ Treaty is a legally binding instrument under the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea for marine biodiversity beyond national jurisdiction.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: The Marine Biodiversity of Areas Beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ) Treaty is an international legally binding instrument under the United Nations Convention, on the Law of the Sea for the conservation and sustainable use of marine biological diversity of areas beyond national jurisdiction.

sections.label: Treaty coverage and global targets
sections.summary: The treaty covers nearly two-thirds of the ocean and supports Sustainable Development Goal 14 and the target to protect 30% by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: The treaty covers nearly two-thirds of the ocean.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: It is an important step towards achieving Sustainable Development Goal 14 – to conserve and sustainably use the oceans, seas and marine resources for sustainable development – as well as the global target to protect 30% of the world's lands, inland waters, coastal areas and oceans by 2030.

sections.label: Equitable benefit sharing and capacity-building
sections.summary: The Treaty addresses inequalities among states by providing equitable sharing of marine scientific research benefits and capacity-building for developing countries.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Second, the Treaty seeks to address some of the inequalities among states in their ability to manage and use the resources of the areas beyond national jurisdiction.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: It provides for greater and more equitable sharing of the benefits arising from marine scientific research in these areas for all countries; and it will boost capacity-building efforts for developing countries to better conserve and to sustainably use their marine biodiversity and to implement this Treaty.

sections.label: Ratification and implementation challenge
sections.summary: After concluding negotiations, the challenge is to get countries to ratify and actually implement the treaty.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: The challenge now, having concluded the negotiations on the text, is to get countries to ratify and, more importantly, to actually implement.

sections.label: Unequal capacities and common rules
sections.summary: Unequal capacities give some countries a head start, so the treaty sets common rules and ensures more equitable distribution of benefits.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Number one, the unequal capacities of countries already cause a challenge.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Because there will be some countries who have the technology and, therefore, have a head start to exploit and gain even sometimes an unfair advantage over others.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: This is one reason why this treaty is so important – because it sets common rules for everyone.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Second, this treaty also ensures that there is a more equitable distribution of the benefits that derive from the extraction and the exploitation of this natural heritage of all of us.
